{{Quote|I believe in the democratization of fear.|Darth Jadus to Cipher Nine|<ref name="DM">{{TORcite|type=class|[[Cipher Nine|Imperial Agent]]|Dark Meeting|[[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]}}</ref>}}
'''Darth Jadus''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]] and a member of the [[Tenebrae|Emperor's]] [[Dark Council]]. Said to be second in power to only the Emperor, Jadus initially concentrated his attention on overseeing the [[Imperial Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Imperial Intelligence]] network, controlling it through various liaisons. Concerned about the future of the Empire due to his fellow Lords' constant civil wars and [[Speciesism/Legends|xenophobia]], Jadus eventually began a secret coup against the Dark Council, seeking to unify the Empire and bring the ways of the Sith directly to its citizens.

==Biography==
===Imperial Intelligence===
{{Quote|This is not your domain, Keeper. It is mine. It has always been mine.|Darth Jadus to Keeper|<ref name="TPLtDK">{{TORcite|type=class|[[Cipher Nine|Imperial Agent]]|The Path Leads to Dromund Kaas|[[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]}}</ref>}}
[[File:Jadus.png|thumb|right|200px|Darth Jadus]]
Jadus was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]. Presumably [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]],<ref name="Holonet" /> located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Jadus rose to prominence among the Sith during the years of the [[Great Galactic War]] and the subsequent [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], securing a position for himself on the Sith's [[Dark Council]] and developing into its most powerful member. The Sith Lord also gained control of the [[Imperial Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Imperial Intelligence]] spy network during the Cold War, working behind the scenes through various intermediaries. At some point he sired a [[Darth Zhorrid|daughter]] who became his only known [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]]. Jadus also commanded the [[Harrower-class dreadnought|Imperial dreadnaught]] [[Dominator (Harrower-class)|''Dominator'']].<ref name="Holonet" />
====An epoch of terror====
In [[3643 BBY]] a new terrorist organization emerged in the Empire, the [[Eagle's network]], which Jadus instructed a [[Cipher Nine|new Intelligence recruit]] to investigate. The terrorists soon launched an attack on the generators powering [[Kaas City]], failing only due to the efforts the agent. A simultaneous attack, however, bombed the ''Dominator'', killing thousands of Imperial dignitaries aboard for a planned cruise across the Empire. Jadus was also on board and thus presumed dead, leading the Dark Council to elect his daughter [[Darth Zhorrid]] as his replacement. Zhorrid ordered Intelligence to use all its resources to find the terrorist leader [[Eagle]] and provide her with revenge.

Imperial Intelligence, thanks to the agent now codenamed [[Cipher Nine]], began disassembling the Eagle's entire network. In the end they found and killed the Eagle himself, who was attempting to use experimental Imperial weapons known as [[Eradicator (weapon)|Eradicators]] to launch a devastating attack on Imperial holdings. Before dying, however, the Eagle revealed that he had a mysterious "Patron" high up within the Empire.

Hunting down this Patron, Cipher Nine discovered it to be Darth Jadus; he had been the real leader of the Eagle terrorists all along. By faking his own death, holding the ''Dominator'' together through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] while [[shvash gas]] incinerated it, he had weakened the Council as they fought each other to claim his resources. He intended to finish the job with the Eradicators, using them against the Empire until it ceased to be ruled by Sith leaders whose infighting he felt was holding it back from its promised rise to glory and strength.

However, in the course of defeating the Eagle, Cipher Nine had obtained half of the Eradicator command codes. Jadus attempted to recruit Nine to execute his plan of firing them, leading to a complicated decision for the agent. Jadus disappeared soon after, his fate unclear. One hypothesis is that Cipher Nine gave him the codes in order to distract him, then sabotaged his ship so the Dark Council and naval reinforcements could move in, and they took him prisoner. Another is that Cipher Nine either talked him down or used the codes to deactivate the Eradicators, with Jadus disappearing once they became useless. Yet another contends that Cipher Nine freely gave him the codes, becoming the "Hand of Jadus." Jadus then tasked the agent with killing his daughter, Zhorrid, so that he could resume his place on the Dark Council and reshape the Empire according to his image.

In any case, Jadus soon left the reaches of [[The galaxy/Legends|the known galaxy]] to better enact his further plans in secret, having also learned of the Emperor's plans to wipe all life from the galaxy.

Years later, he was listed as a potential suspect in orchestrating the [[War on Iokath]] by [[Lana Beniko]], confirming Jadus was still considered alive and pulling hidden strings.

===Exile and reorganization===
After failing to seize control of the Sith Empire, Darth Jadus disappeared into deep space and was widely presumed dead. In reality, he survived in hiding, drawing on the resources and loyal followers he had accumulated during his time leading Imperial Intelligence. From exile, he began quietly rebuilding his influence.<ref name="Return of Jadus" />

While the Republic and the Empire struggled in the aftermath of the Eternal Empire’s [[Eternal Empire conquest|conquest]], Jadus expanded his network across multiple organizations. As instability spread, driven by conflicts such as the [[Mandalorian civil war (Third Galactic War)|Mandalorian civil war]], renewed Republic–Imperial [[Third Galactic War|hostilities]], and Darth Malgus’s [[Malgus's escape|escape]], Jadus used the chaos to conceal his activities while preparing a plan to realize his vision of a galaxy ruled through fear under his authority.<ref name="Return of Jadus" />

At some point, Jadus, without the threat of [[Tenebrae|the Sith Emperor]], learned the secrets of [[Darth Nul]] and her history as both a Jedi and a Sith, including developing a unique understanding that all of Nul's inventions required one key component: Nul's holocron. Jadus knew that the holocron was not only removed from [[Elom/Legends|Elom]] but that the [[Alliance Commander]] was in possession of it but they not only lacked the holocron's true power but also the vision to use it.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

Darth Jadus was also kept contact with [[Darth Rivix]], a Sith Lord and leader of the newly-christened [[Hand of the Empire]] under the [[Darth Acina|new]] [[Darth Vowrawn|leadership]], who in turn was dis-illusuioned as the new leader of the Empire as their grip on the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] was tenuous and that the galaxy deserved a strong leader. Whether this meant that Jadus intended to rule the Empire, as he attempted earlier under different circumstances and using different methods, or the galaxy as a whole is unknown.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

Darth Jadus was also in contact with the Hidden Chain and intended to form an alliance especially since Shae Vizla had allied with [[Darth Malgus]] which brought the two warring Mandalorian factions to a somewhat equal standing. Jadus was also aware that Heta was constructing a full-scale replica of Nul's machine on the abandoned Sith world of [[Khar Shian]] but only had a suspicion as to why that was the case.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

===Return===
====Contacting the Alliance Commander====
{{Quote|Darth Jadus was once the lifeblood of Imperial Intelligence. Near to the Emperor in power and significance. He's been missing, banished... no one knows for certain|[[Lana Beniko]] to the [[Alliance Commander]]|<ref name="Jadus Return" />}}
[[File:Jadus Odessen Message.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Darth Jadus' message to the Eternal Alliance]]
Darth Jadus made his move<ref name="Jadus Return">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|Dark Heart of the Fortress|[[Odessen]]}}</ref> by alerting [[Jekiah Ordo]], who currently leads the Mandalorians in [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae's]] absence, and the [[Alliance Commander]]<ref>{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|Galactic Threads|[[Odessen]]}}</ref> to a droid in need of repairs on [[Elom/Legends|Elom]]<ref>{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|The Library of Nul|[[Elom/Legends|Elom]]}}</ref> and a mysterious call from a person in need of a protector from a potential [[Hidden Chain]] defector on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] both of which Jadus, in a pre-recorded holo-transmission sent to Odessen, praised the Commander for doing well despite him nearly losing his patience.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=general|On the Run|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref>

Jadus reveals that the purpose was to let the Commander know what [[Darth Malgus]] intends to do: utilizing the machine of [[Darth Nul]] on a grander scale thereby reawakening a connection to the Force in many individuals in order to overwhelm both [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] to fundamentally disrupt the order of things. He adds further that [[Heta Kol]] is blind in her own desire to reshape the galaxy is infact hastening towards making Malgus' vision into a reality.<ref name="Jadus Return" />

His message then goes on to state that the Commander and the [[Sa'har Kateen|young Jedi]], in [[Mission to Hidden Chain Ship|taking back]] [[Darth Nul's holocron]], have taken the key piece that will lead to the machine's success or failure. He then shows an image of [[Ri'kan Kateen]] and Sa'har, who is in chains, meeting with Hidden Chain soldiers to which Jadus' message continues by stating that the Commander stands in the way of the inevitable and delaying achieves nothing and that the Commander has a choice: to continue this stalemate or have a say in what is inescapable by heeding Jadus' counsel and have control over what is to come. The message concludes with Jadus telling the Commander to consider their choices carefully and that he would contact them again.<ref name="Jadus Return" />

====True plans revealed====
{{Quote|A shift in power is coming. You have been warned of it, witnessed it, numerous times. Nul's machine is only a part of it. Good intentions are not enough. The only way to preserve the galaxy is tthrough structure. Order. Fear.|Darth Jadus to the [[Alliance Commander]]|<ref name="Masters Enigma" />}}
Darth Jadus once again sent a recorded message to the Alliance Commander to meet him on board [[Enigma (research vessel)|the ''Enigma'']], Nul's research vessel, and to bring [[Darth Nul's holocron]] with them. Jadus had sent his acolytes and troopers to bring his "guests" to the vessel's throne room where Jadus greets them and introduces them to the ''Enigma''.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

Jadus begins by thanking the Commander, and their ally, for responding to his invitation which he marks as an intelligent decision which leads to Jadus. Since their goals were aligned, Jadus offers a collaboration: To stop Heta Kol and her Hidden Chain and to thwart Malgus' plans thereby bringing order to the galaxy. Jadus further states that the machine that was [[Mission to Hidden Chain Ship| destroyed by the Commander]] was merely a prototype and that the Hidden Chain completed a full scale version of Nul's masterpiece. But the goal was to stop Malgus from accessing the machine and that Malgus wasn't the warrior he once was due to now being a broken man obsessed with his own legacy ever since his defeat and subsequent caging. Jadus refers the Commander as the only one that can stop him, because they hold the holocron due to being bound to them. Jadus then makes the ultimatum that the Commander has the holocron but Jadus has the focus and that the holocron's full power must be unlocked using the ''Enigma'' thereby doing what no one else can do. Jadus hopes that the Commander makes the correct choice in this partnership.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

[[File:Jadus_and_Rivix.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Jadus and his forces ambush the Alliance Commander]]
Once the Commander had completed the holocron, Jadus appeared before them with his army and their weapons drawn congratulating them for playing their part well which was a rare commodity. Jadus also reveals to the Commander that [[Khar Shian]] was the location that the Hidden Chain had come close to building Nul's machine and that he was pleased that his efforts were not wasted. With the final component completed, Jadus demands that the Commander relinquish the holocron to them stating that their role was at an end watching as an acolyte approached the holocron only for the Commander to block their path. Jadus further stated that the Commander had the potential to be one of his followers but only his vision would be carried forward by Nul's machine.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

Seeing the Commander ready for a fight, Jadus mused that despite all the power and skills at the Commander's disposal they still failed to recognize the real threat: Betrayal from [[Darth Rivix|Wit]][[Tau Idair|hin]]. Observing at how the Commander's ally had trapped the Commander within a force field that held them in place as the ally gave the holocron to Jadus, Jadus mused that this was how the Commander found defeat after so many victories. The Commander stated that it wasn't over but Jadus retorted saying that it was indeed over and proceeded to leave.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

[[File:Jadus_Departs.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Jadus departs the ''Enigma'']]
When the Commander broke free of their restraints, Jadus used a mysterious Force technique on the Commander where they faced off against visions of their allies, thereby giving Jadus and his followers enough time to reach their ship and prepare to depart the ''Enigma''. Jadus told the Commander that he looked forward to when they and their allies find him on [[Khar Shian]], so that they could bear witness to his ultimate triumph which they cannot stop. The Commander caught up with them but Jadus had prepared his troops nearby to fire on the Commander who made quick work of them and proceeded to destroy one of the engines of Jadus' ship. However Jadus unlocked the force field of the hangar to escape while also attempting to kill the Commander. Jadus' ship left the planet and headed towards his fleet consisting of two [[Harrower-class dreadnought|''Harrower''-class dreadnoughts]] and then departed.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

Later, Jadus contacted [[Heta Kol]] and asked if she was ready to accept his offer thereby uniting his organization with the [[Hidden Chain]].<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:DarthJadus-TOR.png|thumb|right|180px|Darth Jadus]]
{{Quote|He was power, and fire, and brilliance.|Vyord Yanol to Cipher Nine|<ref name="SotDL">{{TORcite|type=class|[[Cipher Nine|Imperial Agent]]|Shadow of the Dark Lord|[[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]}}</ref>}}
A prominent yet enigmatic figure among the Sith, Darth Jadus was known for being cold and brilliant. Showing more self-restraint than his fellow Dark Lords, he rarely succumbed to rage or signs of passion; he kept the emotions that fueled the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] to himself, even hiding his features in a mask that encased his entire face. He showed very little interest in the squabbles and power struggles so common among his fellow Councilors, and in fact saw them as obstacles to the Empire obtaining its full glory.

Choosing instead to focus his influence on the Imperial Intelligence network, Jadus ensured it remained the galaxy's largest espionage organization. He was staunchly opposed to the [[Humanocentrism|anti-alien]] policies of the Empire and freely allowed [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] into Imperial Intelligence, possibly including the agent who would become Cipher Nine.

His enigmatic nature, coupled with his tendency to uplift ordinary citizens and non-Force sensitives rather than other Sith as his favored agents, fostered a sense of unease and distrust among his peers and an almost religious fervor among his servants.<ref name="Holonet" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Damn it, we can't fight him on our own — his power is second to the Emperor's.|Watcher Two to Cipher Nine|<ref name="ANEoF">{{TORcite|type=class|[[Cipher Nine|Imperial Agent]]|A New Epoch of Fear|the ''[[Dominator (Harrower-class)|Dominator]]''}}</ref>}}
As a Dark Council member, Darth Jadus was immensely powerful with the dark side of the Force, capable of [[Teleportation (Force power)/Legends|teleportation]], [[Force choke]], [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], [[Mind trick/Legends|Force corruption]], and [[Force healing/Legends|healing]]. Darth Jadus was also talented with his single-bladed [[Sith lightsaber/Legends|Sith lightsaber]].

Imperial Intelligence employees asserted that Darth Jadus' powers were second only to those of the [[Tenebrae|Emperor]]. This was acknowledged by the Emperor himself, who, in a conversation with Cipher Nine, declared Jadus to be the best Sith his Empire had ever produced despite being deeply flawed.<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire]]''</ref>

Darth Jadus' power was enough to earn the respect and admiration of [[Dread Masters|Dread Master]] [[Raptus]], who revealed to Cipher Nine that Jadus viewed everything in the same way the Dread Masters did.

Those unfortunate enough to find themselves in his presence experienced a physical sensation of pain and suffering due to the power of the dark side radiating from him.

==Behind the scenes==
Darth Jadus was first identified in an [[in-universe]] [[The Holonet|Holonet]] entry on the website for [[BioWare]]'s [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. Included in this entry are [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] phrases such as "Herald of a New Era," "Daughter is only known apprentice," and "Who is the hand of Jadus." He is voiced by [[Stephen Rashbrook]].<ref>''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Legacy of the Sith]]'' {{c|credits}}</ref>

===Gameplay alternatives===
There are three alternate options to Jadus' fate: in the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] option, Cipher Nine can use their codes to deactivate the Eradicators while attempting to fend off Jadus, who leaves once they are shut down, or reason with him before convincing him to go; in the dark side, Nine can choose to enter the codes as a distraction while they sabotage his ship and [[Shara Jenn|Watcher Two]] alerts the Dark Council, who surround his vulnerable vessel, force him to stand down and take him prisoner; in another dark-side option, Cipher Nine can join Jadus, earning the title "Hand of Jadus" and letting him reform Intelligence to his own use.

If Nine chooses to serve Jadus, during the class mission on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], the agent runs into one of [[Lalya Verron|Jadus' servants]], who assigns the agent to survey a detachment of [[Imperial Guard]]smen on the planet. Once the mission is complete, the servant cryptically claims that Jadus now has a better grasp of the Sith Emperor's plans.

Following Chapter 2 of the Imperial Agent story, Jadus tells Cipher Nine that he's removing himself from the war to concentrate on other plans, leaving Nine to carry out his work. He also sanctions the [[Minister of Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Minister of Intelligence's]] request for Nine to hunt down and destroy the [[Star Cabal]], being one of the few Sith to believe Nine about them.

In the storyline ''The Master's Enigma'' which was released with Game Update 7.8.1, there are notable faction outcomes:
* '''Imperial players''' will have '''[[Darth Rivix]]''' as their companion who will then betray the player because he believes that [[Darth Vowrawn|Vowrawn]], or [[Darth Acina|Acina]] depending on the choices made in ''War for Iokath'', are not fit to rule and believes that only the strong should rule and the only one deserving of it is Darth Jadus. Rivix then departs with Jadus.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />
* '''Republic players''' will have '''[[Tau Idair]]''' as their companion who will then betray the player because Jadus has [[Sa'har Kateen]] as his prisoner and Tau is willing to exchange the holocron for Sa'har but Jadus double crosses her by reneging on their deal and knocking Tau out with his [[Force lightning/Legends|lightning]] and takes both an unconscious Tau and the holocron with him. Darth Rivix is seen on Jadus' side in this scenario.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />

As for the outcome differences:
*If the Commander '''accepts''' Jadus' offer, he will then have his guards escort the Commander to the area where they need to begin completing the holocron.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />
*If the Commander '''refuses''' Jadus' offer, then Jadus watches as his guards are cut down by the Commander and their ally then knocking Rivix out with lightning and using a mysterious Force technique on the Commander to knock them out. Both Rivix and the Commander find themselves in the area with no way to retreat.<ref name="Masters Enigma" />
